=== hpc_project ===

  Use command as:
  > hpc  option
  Option: [quota|space]          ==> to list available space and quota
          [q|queue]              ==> to list batch queues and status
          [queue limit]          ==> to list batch queues description and CPU/Mem limits
          [cpu|cores]            ==> to list cpu/cores allowed to use
          [batch|jobs|submit]    ==> to list instruction on batch job submission
          [mpi|mpijob|parallel]  ==> to list instruction on MPI   job submission
          [R|Rjob]               ==> to list instruction on R     job submission
          [DL [batch] ] [volta]  ==> to list instruction on Deep Learning job submission
          [parallel20 ]          ==> to list instruction on using queue < parallel20 >
          [dos|win]              ==> to list instruction on common problem with Windows text file/program
          [hpctmp|workspace]     ==> to list instruction on using HPC workspace /hpctmp.
          [alphafold]            ==> to list instruction on Alphafold job submission

=== hpc_mpi ===

-------------------------------------------------------------------
Steps in submitting and run program a.out with 12 CPU-cores
in batch queue "parallel":

1, Put the following text in a file, eg. myjob1.txt

[1;31m   <<< Script starts from next line. >>> [0m
[1;32m#!/bin/bash [0m
[1;32m#BSUB -q parallel [0m
[1;32m#BSUB -n 12 [0m
[1;32m#BSUB -o stdout_myjob1_%J.o  [0m
[1;32m#BSUB -R "span[ptile=12]"  [0m

[1;32msource /etc/profile.d/modules.sh [0m
[1;32mmodule load mvapich2_gnu [0m

[1;32mmpirun  -np ${LSB_DJOB_NUMPROC}  -f ${LSB_DJOB_HOSTFILE}  ./a.out arg1 arg2 [...] [0m
[1;32mexit 0 [0m

[1;31m   <<< Script ends at the above line. >>> [0m

  Note:   change -n 12 to 24/36/48 if you need to run the program with more cores,
          change queue, output filename, module name, and program name accordingly if needed.
          do not change ptile=12.
  Advice: enter ( nano myjob1.txt ) and copy-paste the above text to edit/save the file.


2, Submit the job as:
[1;32m   #>  bsub < myjob1.txt [0m


3, Check status of job by command:
[1;32m   #>  bjobs [0m

4, To Check the standard output message or progress of job by command:

[1;32m   #>  bpeek  jobid [0m
[1;32m   #>  bpeek2 jobid [0m
-------------------------------------------------------------------


=== end ===
